key_insight: inClinico Agent combines machine-learning trial-success predictions with LLM tools to forecast primary endpoint outcomes across phases I–IV, rather than discover cancer drugs directly.
clinical_relevance: The system could support clinical development prioritization, but the abstract does not establish cancer-specific performance or utility for patient treatment decisions.
method: Train separate models for efficacy and safety/toxicity primary endpoints.
Use registration-time trial features and frozen literature embeddings to reduce outcome leakage.
Integrate probability scores with LLMs, retrieval tools and specialized clinical skills.
evidence_signal: On trials initiated in 2021 or later, AUROC was 0.828 for efficacy (n=2,347) and 0.809 for safety/toxicity (n=1,485); ClinBench tracks predictions for 2,040 ongoing trials.
watch_item: Prospective accuracy remains to be established as ClinBench trials complete; retrospective discrimination alone does not establish probability calibration or decision-making benefit.
paper_title: inClinico Agent for clinical trial endpoint prediction and prospective evaluation
